🇲🇽🏭 30,000 FREE SPOTS — MEXICO'S PUBLIC AI CENTER TRIPLES CAPACITY

Mexico's public AI training center just opened 30,000 spots for its second generation — triple the 10,000 in January's first cohort. Five months, fully online, completely free.

The curriculum spans AI, cybersecurity, cloud computing, data analysis, and 5G infrastructure, with job placement pipelines into NVIDIA, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, AWS, and Intel.

While the US guts public science funding, Mexico is building a free pipeline from zero tech background to employment at the world's biggest tech firms. Registration open through July 5.

🔥🇲🇽 PAN CHOSE FOREIGN INTERVENTION — MORENA LAYS OUT THE RECEIPTS

Morena president Ariadna Montiel laid out the case: PAN leadership "decided to bet on foreign intervention" — hosting Madrid's Díaz Ayuso with four PAN governors, permitting CIA agents in Chihuahua, and coordinating with far-right sectors from Argentina, Spain, and the US.

Montiel added a corruption kicker: PAN leader Jorge Romero allegedly ran the "Real Estate Cartel" in CDMX — 130 illegal buildings, 264 unauthorized floors, over 7.142 billion pesos in damages. "He remains free despite being the cartel's leader."

🇲🇽🔥 341-124: CONGRESS APPROVES JUDICIAL REFORM + FOREIGN INTERFERENCE CLAUSE

Mexico's Chamber of Deputies voted 341-124 to postpone the second judicial election to June 2028 — and approved a new constitutional cause for election nullity: proven foreign interference.

PAN and PRI voted against. The reform also creates a Coordinating Commission to vet judicial candidates. The foreign interference clause arrives as Chihuahua's governor faces impeachment over unauthorized CIA agents operating in her state.

They wanted to interfere. Mexico just made it constitutionally nullifiable.

🇲🇽🌎 TMEC FORMAL TALKS BEGIN — MEXICO SETS THE TABLE

Mexico opened the first formal round of TMEC renegotiations today in Mexico City, with Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard leading the Mexican delegation against US Deputy Trade Rep Jeff Goettman and 60 American business leaders.

Ebrard didn't sugarcoat it — "the conversations are complex and difficult" — but held firm: Mexico opposes the auto tariffs, considers the steel levy unfounded, and pointed out the avocado tariff backfired, boosting Canadian exports to the US instead.

Three rounds mapped out: May 27-29 in Mexico City, June 16-17 in Washington, July 20 back in Mexico. The table is set on Mexican soil first.

SILENCE: Juárez disarmament program + USMCA bilateral talks
May 27 | 🔴

📰 Reuters ran photos from Ciudad Juárez: children trading toy guns for educational toys as part of Mexico's "Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz" program. The government pays $1,200 for an AK-47, $1,300 for a machine gun. The Catholic Church co-runs it. 24 of 31 states have participated.

Zero US editorial coverage. A country actively buying back weapons — 80% of which came from the US — while the US can't pass a background check bill.

Meanwhile, USMCA bilateral talks began May 25 in Mexico City. The US and Mexico are negotiating directly without Canada — Mexico's trade leverage at its highest point in decades. Barely a mention while 15+ cartel and World Cup fear stories ran this week.

BLOOMBERG: Trump's tariffs are pushing Mexico back toward low-value exports
May 27 | 🟡

📰 Bloomberg reports Mexico's export profile is shifting: auto exports stagnate while computer equipment assembly surged 144% last year. The framing: Mexico is regressing toward lower-value goods.

🔍 NAFTA spent 30 years building Mexico into an auto export platform integrated with US supply chains. Now US tariffs are dismantling that integration. Mexico's auto sector employs 800,000 people. Computer assembly employs 60,000. The US built the dependency, broke it, and Bloomberg frames the wreckage as Mexico's problem.

• Auto exports stagnating while computer equipment surged 144%, doubling to 13% of exports
• 800,000 auto jobs vs 60,000 in computer assembly
• April exports hit $72 billion — but composition shifted toward lower-value goods

REUTERS: The paper trail linking a US fuel trader to a notorious Mexican cartel
May 27 | 🟢

📰 Reuters traces Houston fuel company Ikon Midstream directly to CJNG. They shipped 120,000 barrels of diesel to Ensenada, relabeled it as "lubricating oil" to dodge $7 million in Mexican import taxes on a single shipment, and used cartel front companies to receive it.

💀 The FBI raided Ikon's Houston offices in April 2025. 16+ arrests on the Mexican side. US media runs 50 cartel stories a week. Here's one where the supply chain starts in a Houston office park.

• "It is hard to believe that this was an accident" — former CBP director
• CJNG front company "Intanza" received the cargo; buyer "Azteca Cone" had no verifiable business presence
• Fuel misclassified using HTS code 2710.19.3020 to evade import duties

AP / HRW: US has deported thousands of Cubans and Venezuelans to danger in Mexico
May 27 | 🟡

📰 Human Rights Watch documents 13,000 Cubans, Venezuelans, and other nationals deported to Mexico. More than half of interviewed Cubans held green cards and had lived in the US since the 1980s. Some were 83 years old.

The headline says "danger in Mexico." The danger is a 70-year-old green card holder waking up in Tapachula with no money, no contacts, and no judge ever seeing their case.

🇲🇽 None were taken before a judge. 25% had no criminal record. Mexico didn't create this crisis — it was handed one.

• "Imagine being 60 or 70 years old, uprooted from your life overnight and sent to a country you don't know"
• Cubans are the largest group: 4,300+ deported to Mexico because Cuba won't accept them
• Only 16% of deportees had violent criminal histories

THE INTERCEPT: Trump's 'Donroe Doctrine' Supercharges Violence in the Americas
May 27 | 🟢

📰 ACLED, the world's top conflict tracker, just published the receipts on the Donroe Doctrine.

195 civilians killed in US boat strikes since September 2025. Security forces across the hemisphere killed 6,900 people in one year — highest since 2018. Cartel drone attacks in Mexico up 567% from 2023 to 2025.

🔍 The Intercept names the CIA operations in Mexico, "Operation Total Extermination" in Ecuador, the strikes on civilian boats. Ecuador went from 24 gangs to 37 after US-backed leader takedowns. Every capture splinters the group.

• "U.S. pressure on organized crime is accelerating the spread of militarized security approaches in the region"
• 59 attacks on boats since September 2025, killing 195 civilians
• Ecuador's gangs grew from 24 to 37 after leader captures

🇲🇽🏭 SLIM CALLS MOODY'S DOWNGRADE "IRRATIONAL" — ANNOUNCES $5 BILLION MEXICO INVESTMENT

Carlos Slim dismissed Moody's Baa2-to-Baa3 downgrade as "irrational" at his annual press conference, arguing rating agencies ignore the capital actually entering the country.

Then he backed it with action: $5 billion in 2026 investment across infrastructure, energy — including the Ixachi oil field with 32 active wells producing 2,000 barrels/day — and telecommunications. Mexico posted record FDI of $23.59 billion in Q1 2026, up 10% year-over-year.
